name: recyclebin_i
description: Parse $Recycle.Bin $I metadata (version 1 and 2 records, unsigned fields): the original path, original size and deletion time (raw FILETIME and ISO 8601 UTC with seven fractional digits), for one file or every $I under a directory in sorted order. Every length is checked against the bytes the file has: a record shorter than its layout needs is reported truncated with the bytes it has and the path decoded from them as far as it goes, never as a complete one; a longer one carries trailing_bytes; a file over 1 MiB is not read (it is not a $I); an unknown header is not guessed at. Every candidate is checked as it is found and opened without blocking and without following a link: a $I that is a link, a FIFO, a device, a socket or a directory is not opened and is counted in not_attempted (each with its entry and the reason, status partial), a directory that cannot be listed is an entry too, and a link to a directory is not followed (a path that is itself a link to a directory is refused). Nothing here can hang on a FIFO or lose the rest of the bin. The whole record is read, not a fixed 4096 bytes. Each entry names its $R counterpart where present and the SID of the bin directory it sits in. The bin's SID is the account whose bin received the item; it does not say who deleted the file or from where.

path.description: A $I file, or a directory holding them

limit.description: Entries shown inline (default 500, an inline page size); every entry is kept, and when there are more the whole list is written as JSON Lines and named in all_results
